questions.question: A shopkeeper bought 288 oranges for Rs. 115.20. He sold 50 of them at 70 paise each and the remaining at Rs. 46.20. Find his profit or loss.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total **Cost Price (CP)** = Rs. 115.20.

**Selling Price (SP)** of 50 oranges = 50 × 0.70 = Rs. 35.

**SP** of remaining oranges = Rs. 46.20.

Total **SP** = 35 + 46.20 = Rs. 81.20.

Since **CP > SP**, it is a **Loss**.

**Loss** = 115.20 − 81.20 = Rs. 34.

**∴ The correct answer is Loss, Rs. 34.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → Total Oranges = **288**, Total CP = **Rs. 115.20**, Rate of 50 oranges = **70 paise** (Rs. 0.70), SP of rest = **Rs. 46.20**.
Formulas: Loss = CP − SP | Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2fa018a4d94506c623b7dcf08b1aa7a4ffeca181c1a1475a9ba8f76df7f123b1.png] 
⇒ Calculate SP of first part: 50 × 0.70 = **Rs. 35**.
⇒ Total SP = SP₁ + SP₂ = 35 + 46.20 = **Rs. 81.20**.
⇒ Loss = CP − SP = 115.20 − 81.20 = **Rs. 34**.

**∴ The correct answer is Loss, Rs. 34.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

When **Selling Price** is greater than **Cost Price**, the merchant makes a **Profit**. Conversely, if **Cost Price** is greater, it results in a **Loss**.

Unit Conversion

Always ensure all values are in the same unit. Here, 70 paise was converted to **Rs. 0.70** (100 paise = Rs. 1).</p

questions.question: If Δ ABC ~ Δ QRP; area of Δ ABC : area of Δ PQR = 9 : 4; AB = 18 cm and BC = 15 cm, then find the length of PR.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Δ ABC ~ Δ QRP

Area of Δ ABC : Area of Δ PQR = 9 : 4

AB = 18 cm

BC = 15 cm

**Formula Used:**

Ratio of the areas of two similar triangles = (Ratio of the corresponding sides)²

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e056f7cd7d92272fba9098e95f7418cb886f4be71565fcd3158aecfd48fec1f3.png] 

Let the ratio of the corresponding sides of Δ ABC and Δ QRP be k.

Then, k² = (9)/(4)

⇒ k = sqrt{(9)/(4)}

⇒ k = (3)/(2)

Since Δ ABC ~ Δ QRP, the corresponding sides are proportional.

We need to find the length of PR which corresponds to BC.

Let PR = x cm.

Then, (BC)/(PR) = (3)/(2)

⇒ (15)/(x) = (3)/(2)

⇒ 15 × 2 = 3 × x

⇒ 30 = 3x

⇒ x = (30)/(3)

⇒ x = 10 cm

**The length of PR is 10 cm.**

questions.question:
Simplify the following expression. 

[40 - 48 ÷ 4 of 3] ÷ {(6 + 4) - 4 of 4 + 4 + (6 - 4) + (4 × 4) ÷ 4} × 3.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Simplify the following expression:

[40 - 48 ÷ 4 of 3] ÷ {(6 + 4) - 4 of 4 + 4 + (6 - 4) + (4 × 4) ÷ 4} × 3.

**Formula Used:**

Order of operations (BODMAS/BIDMAS):

Brackets, Orders (i.e., powers and square roots, etc.), Division and Multiplication (left-to-right), Addition and Subtraction (left-to-right).

**Calculation:**

First, simplify the expression inside the brackets:

⇒ 40 - 48 ÷ 4 of 3

Order of operations dictates we handle division and multiplication first:

⇒ 40 - 48 ÷ (4 × 3)

⇒ 40 - 48 ÷ 12

⇒ 40 - 4

⇒ 36

Next, simplify the expression inside the curly braces:

⇒ (6 + 4) - 4 of 4 + 4 + (6 - 4) + (4 × 4) ÷ 4

Handle multiplication and division first:

⇒ (6 + 4) - 4 × 4 + 4 + (6 - 4) + (16) ÷ 4

⇒ 10 - 16 + 4 + 2 + 4

Perform addition and subtraction from left to right:

⇒ 10 - 16 + 4 + 2 + 4

⇒ -6 + 4 + 2 + 4

⇒ -2 + 2 + 4

⇒ 0 + 4

⇒ 4

Now, substitute these simplified values back into the main expression:

⇒ 36 ÷ 4 × 3

Perform division and multiplication from left to right:

⇒ 9 × 3

⇒ 27

**The correct answer is option 3.**

questions.question: Find the total amount of debt that will be discharged by 5 equal instalments of ₹200 each, if the debt is due in 5 years at 5% p.a. at simple interest.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the annual instalment be 100%.

Total Debt is the sum of future values of all instalments at simple interest.

Total Debt = 100% + 105% + 110% + 115% + 120% = 550% of the instalment.

Given, 100% = ₹200.

Total Debt = 550% of ₹200 = 5.5 × 200 = ₹1100.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Instalment (I) = ₹200

Rate of Interest (R) = 5% p.a.

Time (T) = 5 years

 + 4 yrs @ 5%
 ₹240

 
 Year 2
 ₹200

 + 3 yrs @ 5%
 ₹230

 
 Year 3

 + 2 yrs @ 5%
 ₹220

 
 Year 4
 ₹200

 + 1 yr @ 5%
 ₹210

 
 Year 5
 ₹200

 Final Payment
 ₹200

 
 
• 
 Total Debt Discharged =
 ₹1100
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1st instalment future value = 200 + (200 × 5 × 4) ÷ 100 = ₹240

⇒ 2nd instalment future value = 200 + (200 × 5 × 3) ÷ 100 = ₹230

⇒ 3rd instalment future value = 200 + (200 × 5 × 2) ÷ 100 = ₹220

⇒ 4th instalment future value = 200 + (200 × 5 × 1) ÷ 100 = ₹210

⇒ 5th instalment future value = ₹200 (Paid at maturity, no interest)

⇒ Total Debt = 240 + 230 + 220 + 210 + 200 = ₹1100

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Instalment Formula

Total Debt = I × T + [I × R × T(T − 1)] ÷ 200, where I is the instalment amount, R is rate %, and T is time in years.

Understanding Debt vs Principal

The "Debt" mentioned in simple interest instalment questions represents the total future amount due at maturity (Principal + total accrued Interest), not the initially borrowed sum.

Compound Interest Instalments

For Compound Interest, the relationship calculates the present value of instalments: Principal = I ÷ (1 + R/100) + I ÷ (1 + R/100)² + ... + I ÷ (1 + R/100)T.

questions.question: A and B, working together, take 15 days to complete a piece of work. If A alone can do this work in 18 days, then how long would B take to complete the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A and B together complete the work in 15 days.

A alone completes the work in 18 days.

**Formula Used:**

Work rate of A = 1/Time taken by A

Work rate of B = 1/Time taken by B

Combined work rate of A and B = Work rate of A + Work rate of B

**Calculation:**

Work rate of A = 1/18

Work rate of A and B together = 1/15

Let the time taken by B alone to complete the work be B days.

Work rate of B = 1/B

Combined work rate of A and B:

1/18 + 1/B = 1/15

Solving for B:

⇒ 1/18 + 1/B = 1/15

⇒ 1/B = 1/15 - 1/18

⇒ 1/B = (18 - 15) / (15 × 18)

⇒ 1/B = 3 / 270

⇒ 1/B = 1 / 90

⇒ B = 90

**B alone would take 90 days to complete the same work.**

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks an article at Rs. 150 and sells it at a discount of 25%. He also gives a gift worth Rs. 2.5. If he still makes a 10% profit, then the cost price (in Rs.) of the article is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹150

Discount = 25% of ₹150 = ₹37.50

Gift worth = ₹2.50

Profit = 10%

**Formula used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP - Discount - Gift worth

Profit = SP - Cost Price (CP)

Profit% = ((SP - CP))/(CP) × 100

SP = CP + Profit

**Calculation:**

⇒ SP = ₹150 - ₹37.50 - ₹2.50

⇒ SP = ₹110

⇒ Profit% = ((SP - CP))/(CP) × 100

⇒ 10% = ((110 - CP))/(CP) × 100

⇒ (1)/(10) = ((110 - CP))/(CP)

⇒ CP = 1100 - 10 CP

⇒ 11CP = 1100

⇒ CP = ₹100

**∴ The cost price of the article is ₹100.**

questions.question: Let C be a circle with Centre O and P be an external point to C. Let PQ and PR be the tangents to C such that Q and R be the points of tangency, respectively. If ∠ROQ = 110°, find ∠RPQ.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Centre of the circle, O

External point, P

PQ and PR are tangents to the circle at Q and R respectively

∠ROQ = 110°

**Formula Used:**

∠PQR = 90° and ∠PRQ = 90° (radius of a circle and a tangent line are always perpendicular to each other)

Sum of all angles of Quadrilateral = 360°

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2317074d95d312dc9ed6143a828c9218ac2350098401531c70a9971d92aa47a2.png] 

∠ROQ = 110°

Using the formula:

∠ROQ + ∠PQR + ∠PRQ + ∠RPQ = 360°

⇒ 110° + 90° + 90° +∠RPQ = 360°

⇒ ∠RPQ = 360° - 290°

⇒ ∠RPQ = 70°

**The correct answer is option 3:** 70°

questions.question: An iron box with external dimensions 60 cm, 40 cm, and 20 cm is made of 1 cm thick sheet. If 1 cm³ of iron weighs 50 gm, the weight of the empty box is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**External Volume** = 60 × 40 × 20 = 48,000 cm³

**Internal dimensions** (subtracting 2 cm from each): 58, 38, 18

**Internal Volume** = 58 × 38 × 18 = 39,672 cm³

**Volume of Iron** = 48,000 − 39,672 = 8,328 cm³

**Weight** = 8,328 × 50 gm = 416,400 gm = 416.40 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 416.40 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** External Length (L) = 60 cm, Breadth (B) = 40 cm, Height (H) = 20 cm. Thickness (t) = 1 cm. Density = 50 gm/cm³.

**Formula:** Volume of material = External Volume − Internal Volume

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/06079ee345ae6dd077aacd1d508552180d83c307a96317163fce2990bc7d5210.png] 

⇒ **External Volume** = 60 × 40 × 20 = 48,000 cm³

⇒ **Internal Length (l)** = 60 − (2 × 1) = 58 cm

⇒ **Internal Breadth (b)** = 40 − (2 × 1) = 38 cm

⇒ **Internal Height (h)** = 20 − (2 × 1) = 18 cm

⇒ **Internal Volume** = 58 × 38 × 18 = 39,672 cm³

⇒ **Volume of Iron** = 48,000 − 39,672 = 8,328 cm³

⇒ **Weight in gm** = 8,328 × 50 = 416,400 gm

⇒ **Weight in kg** = 416,400 ÷ 1,000 = 416.40 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 416.40 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of Cuboid

The volume of a **cuboid** is calculated as Length × Breadth × Height.

Hollow Cuboid Dimensions

For a **hollow box** with thickness 't', the internal dimension is (External Dimension − 2t).

Weight and Density

**Weight** = Volume × Density. Always ensure units are consistent (1 kg = 1000 gm).</p

questions.question:
Study the given bar-graph and answer the question that follows. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/799e5541bcb977f212c736ea9504240a358423d9dfa0558f27be0d66557e73bb.png] 

How many students obtained more than the average marks of the class?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The bar graph shows the distribution of marks obtained by students.

**Formula Used:**

1. Average marks = Total marks / Total number of students

2. Number of students who obtained more than the average marks.

**Calculation:**

**Step 1: Calculate total marks and total number of students**

Total students = 1 + 3 + 2 + 8 + 5 + 4 + 1 = 24

Total marks = (1 × 125) + (3 × 130) + (2 × 135) + (8 × 140) + (5 × 145) + (4 × 150) + (1 × 160) = 125 + 390 + 270 + 1120 + 725 + 600 + 160 = 3390

**Step 2: Calculate the average marks**

Average marks ⇒ 3390 / 24 ≈ 141.25

**Step 3: Find the number of students who obtained more than the average marks**

Students who scored above 141.25 are those who scored 145, 150, and 160 marks.

Number of students in these categories: 5 (145 marks) + 4 (150 marks) + 1 (160 marks) = 10

**Therefore, 10 students obtained more than the average marks of the class.**

questions.question: The perimeter of a triangle is 36 units. Its area cannot be more than ______ square units.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Perimeter of the triangle = 36 units

**Formula used:**

Area of a triangle with maximum possible area is of equilateral triangle.

Maximum area of an equilateral triangle = (side²) × (√3)/(4)

For an equilateral triangle, side = (Perimeter)/(3)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Side = 36 / 3 = 12 units

⇒ Area = (12)² × (√3)/(4)

⇒ Area = 144 × (√3)/(4)

⇒ Area = 36√3 square units

**∴ The maximum area is 36√3 square units, so the correct answer is Option 2.**

questions.question: A policeman received information that a thief is at a distance of 1.5 km from him. The thief starts moving by car and the policeman chases him by car. The thief and the policeman are moving at the speeds of 90 km/h and 120 km/h respectively. At what distance (in km) will the police catch the thief?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance between policeman and thief = 1.5 km

Speed of the thief = 90 km/h

Speed of the policeman = 120 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Relative speed = Speed of policeman - Speed of thief

Distance = Relative speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Relative speed = 120 km/h - 90 km/h

Relative speed = 30 km/h

Let the time taken to catch the thief be t hours.

Distance covered by the policeman in time t = Distance covered by the thief in time t + Initial distance

120t = 90t + 1.5

⇒ 120t - 90t = 1.5

⇒ 30t = 1.5

⇒ t = 1.5 / 30

⇒ t = 0.05 hours

Distance at which the policeman catches the thief = Speed of policeman × Time

Distance = 120 km/h × 0.05 hours

Distance = 6 km

**The police will catch the thief at a distance of 6 km.**

questions.question: If θ is an acute angle and tan θ + cot θ = 2, then find the value of tan³ θ + cot³ θ + 6tan³ θ cot² θ.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If **tan θ + cot θ = 2**, this condition is only satisfied when **tan θ = 1** and **cot θ = 1** (since θ = 45°).

Substitute **tan θ = 1** and **cot θ = 1** in the required expression:

Expression = 1³ + 1³ + 6 × 1³ × 1²

Expression = 1 + 1 + 6 = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f8fc21ce1f77e8eb80d753ad4c647fd8528087ee31707968acf70d02c4e058ec.png] 

**Given:** tan θ + cot θ = 2

**Formula Used:** cot θ = 1/tan θ and (a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b)

⇒ tan θ + 1/tan θ = 2

⇒ tan² θ + 1 = 2 tan θ

⇒ tan² θ − 2 tan θ + 1 = 0

⇒ (tan θ − 1)² = 0

⇒ tan θ = 1

⇒ cot θ = 1/1 = 1

Now, calculate: tan³ θ + cot³ θ + 6tan³ θ cot² θ

⇒ (1)³ + (1)³ + 6(1)³(1)²

⇒ 1 + 1 + 6 = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Reciprocal Trig Identities

tan θ × cot θ = 1. Similarly, sin θ × cosec θ = 1 and cos θ × sec θ = 1.

Special Case for x + 1/x

If x + 1/x = 2, then xⁿ + 1/xⁿ is always 2 for any positive integer n.

Standard Trig Values

For θ = 45°, tan 45° = 1 and cot 45° = 1. This is the only acute angle satisfying tan θ + cot θ = 2.</p

**Total Time in hours** = 140 ÷ 60 = 7/3 hours

**Average Speed** = 80 ÷ (7/3) = 240/7 = 34(2/7) km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 34(2/7) km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f3f6df9033f049655ad95e72d4ea1cf199506c02d37b6922b764fbfba4aebbcc.png] 

**Given:**

Distance₁ = 50 km, Time₁ = 90 min

Rest Time = 15 min

Distance₂ = 30 km, Time₂ = 35 min

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 50 km + 30 km = 80 km

⇒ Total Time = 90 + 15 + 35 = 140 minutes

⇒ Conversion to hours: 140/60 hours = 7/3 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 80 ÷ (7/3)

⇒ Average Speed = (80 × 3) ÷ 7 = 240/7

⇒ Average Speed = 34(2/7) km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 34(2/7) km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed with Rest

When rest time is included in the journey, it must be added to the total time taken to find the overall average speed for the whole journey.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert time from minutes to hours, divide by 60.

Special Case: Equal Distances

If a person covers two equal distances at speeds V₁ and V₂, the average speed = (2 × V₁ × V₂) ÷ (V₁ + V₂).</p

questions.question: Two quantities are in the ratio 3 : 5. If the first quantity is 155 kg. Find the other quantity (approximately).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratio of quantities = 3 : 5

First quantity = 155 kg

**Formula used:**

Let the second quantity be x.

Ratio = First quantity / Second quantity

**Calculation:**

⇒ (3)/(5) = (155)/(x)

⇒ x = 155 × (5)/(3)

⇒ x ≈ 258.3 kg

**∴ The other quantity is approximately 258.3 kg.**

 left{(3³+2³)times (22)/(7)right}times {(6²+3²-4²)div (14(1)/(2))}
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Expression: {(3³ + 2³) × 22/7} × {(6² + 3² - 4²) ÷ (14 1/2)}

**Formula Used:**

1. Cube of a number: n³

2. Square of a number: n²

3. Mixed fraction: Convert mixed fraction to improper fraction

**Calculation:**

**Step 1: Simplify inside the brackets**

Calculate 3³: ⇒ 3³ = 27

Calculate 2³: ⇒ 2³ = 8

Add them together: ⇒ 27 + 8 = 35

**Step 2: Multiply by 22/7**

Calculate: ⇒ 35 × 22/7 = 5 × 22 = 110

**Step 3: Simplify the second part**

Calculate 6²: ⇒ 6² = 36

Calculate 3²: ⇒ 3² = 9

Calculate 4²: ⇒ 4² = 16

Subtract and add: ⇒ 36 + 9 - 16 = 29

Convert mixed fraction 14(1)/(2) to improper fraction: ⇒ 14(1)/(2) = 29/2

Divide: ⇒ 29 ÷ 29/2 = 29 × 2/29 = 2

**Step 4: Multiply the results from Step 2 and Step 3**

Final calculation: ⇒ 110 × 2 = 220

**Therefore, the simplified value of the given expression is 220.**
